This is a personal blog with entries reflecting my professional interests in computer languages and data analysis and visualization.

Most of my professional experience has been developing Engineering applications using Matlab for modelling and C++ for library implementation. I also like R and Python, however, strongly typed and more declarative programming languages win the day for me. I have way too many books on Haskell, a language that have formed me in many ways. More recently, my focus is on Rust. It brings type safety and an ecosystem of tooling and libraries for just about anything. Now I can enjoy functional programming and safety in a bundle just as comfortable for systems programming as for UI or embedded programming.

In the last 5 years, after completing a Masters degree in Software Engineering at the University of Calgary I have had the chance to design and use relational and document (also called noSQL) databases for work and in a research project.

I am an efficient Linux bash programmer. One has to choose the right tool for the job, bash is so full of tricks and even holes, but it is so good to have a direct connection to the GNU-Linux operating system, bash gives me the power of starting a child process or forking a sub-shell, depending on what I want to achieve.

There are way too many good blogs on Python. I write a lot on R because it is a vectorized language with and awesome expressive power, almost like a Lisp dialect but without the parenthesis. I want to write more on Rust because I think it is a technology that is changing for the better the way we build software infrastructure.
